Overflow does not crash. An int that passes 2.1 × 109 silently becomes a wrong number. When in doubt, use long long and write constants as 100000LL .

title: 顺序结构程序设计案例

text: Read, compute, print: complete worked programs.
Time problems: convert every time to minutes since midnight, compute, then convert back with / 60 and % 60 . Going back past midnight needs the % 1440 + 1440 wrap. The idea behind P1425 and P5707.
What each verdict means, and a checklist before you submit.
After you submit, the judge runs your program on hidden tests and gives a verdict for each. Each verdict points to a different kind of mistake, so read it before changing code.

Verdict Meaning Usual causes AC Accepted — WA Wrong Answer misread rule, overflow, wrong format (spaces, newlines, decimals), missed edge case TLE Time Limit Exceeded algorithm too slow for the limits, infinite loop, slow input/output MLE Memory Limit Exceeded arrays far too big, endless recursion storing data RE Runtime Error index out of range, division by 0, stack overflow from deep recursion CE Compile Error syntax error, a function the judge's compiler lacks, wrong language chosen Self-check before submitting
1. Re-read the statement and the limits; estimate the operation count.
2. Run all samples; compare the output character by character.
3. Test the smallest case (n = 1, 0, empty) and the largest values.
4. Check every product and sum for overflow; use long long .
5. Remove debug output; check spaces, newlines and decimals.
6. Compile with -Wall and read every warning.

Print debug values to cerr : you see them on screen, but they are not part of the answer the judge reads (the Output panel above shows only cout ). Still, remove them before submitting, because printing takes time.
WA on a hidden test while the samples pass usually means an edge case or overflow. Make a tiny test where you know the answer by hand, and compare.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Default to long long; write constants as 100000LL; overflow is silent.
2. A char is a number: c - '0', c - 'a' + 'A'.
3. Convert before dividing: double(a) / b; int(x) cuts toward 0.
4. printf: %lld, %.2f, %02d; cout: fixed << setprecision(k), setw, setfill.
5. Times: convert to minutes; wrap with (t % 1440 + 1440) % 1440.
6. WA: format, overflow, edge cases. TLE: too slow or slow IO. RE: index or /0. CE: syntax.
7. Debug with cerr, remove before submitting; test n = 1 and the largest values.
